title: RAW Carmina 19 gift judgment with equal courtesy, recipient/time screening and bounded generosity
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_EXECUTED. Cached complete Carmina19 offers a connected moral argument: prodigality does not cancel avarice; temperance considers a mean; equal pleasant manner to all coexists with selecting worthy gift recipients and the time; giving improperly is only conditionally good; generosity must not be dissipated. Wheat/chaff and generosity oil are metaphors within gift judgment, not a botanical preparation recipe. No Voynich target or existing whole-form interpretation has been examined; 0 confirmed meanings. Retain as source-only raw content proposal pending primary predecessor and target review.

content_constraints.relation: One opposed vice does not redeem the other; the argument prescribes temperance between both.

content_constraints.span: Vultu licet hilari, verbo licet blando sis equalis omnibus
content_constraints.relation: Equal pleasant face and speech toward all is permitted; it is not universal indiscriminate gift allocation.
Recipient worthiness must be considered before seeking glory through giving.

content_constraints.span: primum videas granum inter paleas, cui des et quando
content_constraints.relation: First discriminate grain among chaff: to whom to give and when. Context supports a recipient/time judgment metaphor; it supplies no literal grain recipe.

content_constraints.span: Dare non ut convenit non est a virtute, bonum est secundum quid, sed non absolute
content_constraints.relation: Improper giving is not virtuous; its goodness is qualified rather than absolute.

content_constraints.span: sed caveto, dum das, largitatis oleum male non effundas
content_constraints.relation: Giving must preserve generosity against waste; oil remains metaphorical in this moral argument.
